Is there any way other than an antivirus scan to be able to see if your computer is one of the bots?

The other way you might notice is if you're familiar with using a network traffic analyzer (like WireShark) and know what's normal traffic on your network, and what's not. Even when you're not really using it, your computer generates network traffic fairly regularly (letting the router know it's still there, checking for software updates, downloading email in the background, syncing your dropbox folder, whatever). So if you look at your network traffic regularly and are used to what it should look like, then you'll recognize if something new starts showing up a lot. There's some software that does this 'watching' automatically and flags things it thinks are suspicious, but it's usually marketed towards enterprise users - antivirus and your OS' built-in firewall are usually enough if you're not the type to open every email attachment that hits your inbox.

That's a considerable part of why it's important to do your system updates and keep your antivirus updated, though - most hijack methods utilize exploits that have already been discovered and patched, and the baddies are just counting on people not having kept their system up to date.

This may be a dumb question. But what exactly is a DDOS attack.
This was helpful to me earlier today: http://www.digitalattackmap.com/understanding-ddos/

DDoS is short for 'Distributed Denial of Service'. A DDoS attack is basically when a large amount of computers (I'm talking several thousand) send useless requests to a server over and over again to try and use up all its resources, thus preventing it from doing its primary job (hence the denial of service part). These computers are usually under control by malicious software and the user of the infected computer may have no clue that they are DDoSing a site.

EDIT: Added punctuation

Distributed Denial of Service attack. You infect a bunch of computers around the world with botware, then when you want to ddos some IP address you make all the computers you infected try to connect to it over and over. I've heard you can buy bots for your botnet that way you don't have to infect a bunch of computers yourself.

Working right now and playing around with Voat for the first time. Ask me anything you want about bail bonds!

What is the most exciting part of your job?

What is the most mindnumbingly boring part of your job?

Being a bondsman is not at all like the shows that you see on TV. 95% of the job is sitting behind a desk in an office and evaluating risk. "Qualifying bonds." Trying to decide whether a person will go to court or not and negotiating collateral as such. A couple times every year we all put on our bullet proof vests and have to go kick down a door to drag somebody back to jail. A good bondsman doesn't have to do this often. We write good bonds. We hold sufficient collateral. We talk the person in. But once in a while you have to go out and risk your life to protect the agency owner's wallet (I'm a non-liable agent/licensed independent contractor). So obviously it is not something that we like to do. The Jail is in a pretty rough area of town (I'm in Orlando) and we get some characters walking in off the street every now and then. Again, not fun to have to kick a belligerent transient out of the office but I suppose it keeps things interesting.

Does it ever make financial sense to go through a bondsman or is it basically for people strapped for cash? If it did make sense to go through a bondsman, would the bondsman accept the case (or whatever you call it)?

Good question! It absolutely does make financial sense to use a bondsman and here's why: There are two ways to get someone out of jail. Let's say my brother was arrested and he was a $1,000 bond. I can bring a money order to the jail for $1,000 or I can use a bondsman and pay $100. The jail returns the money at the end of the case. We don't. But here's the thing, the jail deducts court costs, fees, fines, costs of prosecution, public defender application fee, anything and everything they can think of gets deducted. This is how the county makes money from bonds so they love to eat this up. Oftentimes I'll see the judge set the fines at the EXACT amount of the cash bond. If you use a bondsman, we have nothing to do with any of those fees. Fees and fines are the responsibility of the defendant. So in our example, I would prefer my brother to pay his own court costs. I would prefer the judge set a fine based on the specific case and not the bond amount. There are many reasons why using a bail bondsman is in everyone's best interest. We arent one of those businesses that cater to poor people and help keep people in poverty like cash advance businesses, pawn shops, or rent to own stores.
